annotation.authors_or_issuer: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology (UK Government)
key_provisions_or_claims: Proposes five cross-sector principles: safety/security/robustness; transparency and explainability; fairness; accountability and governance; contestability and redress.
Relies on existing sector regulators to implement the principles on a non-statutory basis, with context-based rather than technology-based regulation.
Creates central government functions to monitor, coordinate and adapt the framework and assess cross-economy risks.
Supports AI sandboxes, testbeds and technical assurance tools and standards to enable trustworthy AI.
Commits to international interoperability and engagement; consults on liability, foundation models and sandboxes.
annotation.summary_en: UK Government white paper (CP 815, March 2023) setting out a pro-innovation, context-based, non-statutory approach to AI regulation. Existing regulators apply five cross-sector principles, supported by central coordination, monitoring, sandboxes and assurance tools, with a consultation on implementation.
annotation.title_clean: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation
annotation.title_en: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation
